    • Everything you reach with a pasted key is one list on the Connections tab, under Apps. Meeting recorders had a tab of their own and GoHighLevel had no place on the tab at all, so connecting a CRM meant going and finding the add-on that wanted one.
    • Reconnect opens inside the row you pressed it on. It used to open a panel at the top of the list, so pressing Reconnect on the fourth mailbox opened something over the first one, and the only way to tell what you had pressed was to read the address in the heading.
    • A connection that nothing installed can use now says so, with an amber dot on the Connections tab and on the sidebar beside it. The add-ons that would use it are buttons you can press right there, instead of a trip to the store to look up what you have just been told.
    • Fireflies, lemlist and GoHighLevel have their own logos in the list. They wore two-letter monograms beside twenty real logos, which read as three services that had failed to load.
    • Response quality now reaches the part of your agent that reads mail and texts in the background. That part was pinned to the middle setting whatever you had chosen, so somebody who moved the dial to Economy to spend less went on paying the middle price on every message that arrived, and no screen said so. Deciding what a message is amounts to sorting the mail, and sorting is what the cheaper settings are for.
    • There is a second number beside "Tell me about at most", called "Read at most". The first one is about your attention. The second is about your money, because working out what a message is costs a little whether or not it turns out to be worth telling you about, and nothing counted that before. Neither one ever holds up a Draft button you pressed yourself.
    • The Spending screen can name what used to land in "Everything else", which was about half of every call your agent made. A row called everything else is only useful when it is the small one.
    • Your agent pays less to read the same mail. A reply carries every earlier message in the thread underneath it, and your agent was being handed all of it every time. The quoted part comes off first now, so what it reads is the message somebody actually just sent.
    • Routines that come due in the same minute run one after another instead of all at once, which makes every one after the first cheaper.
    • The chat says what a model sounds like when it is wrong, under the box rather than in the transcript. Being right and being wrong sound identical coming out of one: no hedge, no hesitation, nothing in the words to go on.
    • Fixed: Response quality had quietly stopped existing for every add-on installed from the store. It survived only on skills you write yourself, so a setting the app describes in three places was adjustable on almost nothing.
    • Fixed: an Outlook mailbox could report itself as broken when it was only busy. Outlook allows one app four requests against a mailbox at a time, and a twenty-message list went out as twenty at once, so the mailbox refused and your agent handed you the refusal as an account problem and named the address, which invited you to reconnect something that was never broken.
    • Fixed: an add-on that names the one service it needs was handed every key on your agent instead of that one. An add-on that names nothing still reaches everything, which is what an add-on you write yourself does.
    • Fixed: starting a new agent from an existing one copied connections belonging to somebody who is not on the new agent, which left keys nobody there could use.
    • Fixed: the remove button could fall off the end of a mailbox row.
    • Fixed: on Windows, the video add-ons downloaded an old copy of one of the tools they need, so they did not run.
    • Fixed: on Windows, setting up phone access rebuilt everything every time it checked, because it could not tell that nothing had changed since the last check.
    Archie 0.1.8August 26, 2026
    • Your agent can tell you about mail it is not going to answer. Email Manager has a new setting for what reaches you: only mail that needs a reply, which is what it did before and is still what a new install does; anything a real person wrote; or everything your ignore list did not drop. Until now, mail your agent decided needed no reply was dropped without a word, so a decision that went wrong looked exactly like an agent that had stopped working.
    • Email Replies is now called Email Manager. Answering is one of the three things it does, beside watching what arrives and filing it away, alongside answering.
    • Its settings are in six named groups instead of one long column, and every on-off setting is a switch at the end of its row instead of a tick box.
    • An email your agent is not handing you a draft for now gets two or three sentences instead of one line, and they carry the date, amount or deadline that was in the message.
    • Your ignore list and the limit on how many messages an hour your agent sends you are visible even when automatic drafts are off. Both were being applied the whole time, from boxes you could not see.
    • Times your agent writes for somebody else say which zone they are in. A reply offering "9am" left the person reading it to work out whether that meant your morning or theirs.
    • Installing an add-on no longer asks you something you have already told this agent. An answer you gave once is filled in for the next add-on that asks the same question.
    • You can stop one agent reading the web. On that agent's page, under Response quality, "Don't let this agent read the web" turns off opening pages and searching, for that agent and for every skill you install later. Email, calendar and chat keep working, and so do the services you connected yourself on the Connections tab. Worth turning on if the computer running Archie belongs to your work.
    • Fixed: every question you asked about an Outlook mailbox failed before it left Archie. Asking whether a message had arrived from somebody sent Outlook a request in a shape it rejects, and your agent then reported the mailbox as unreadable and named the address, which invited you to reconnect an account that was never broken. Watching an Outlook inbox was never affected, which is how both could be true on the same account at the same time.
    • Fixed: the list of who can message your agent could show a stranger's phone number under your own name. A Telegram account id is ten digits, the same shape as a phone number here, so it was drawn as one. The number was real, and it belonged to somebody who has never heard of Archie.
    • Fixed: your agent could be watching no inboxes at all while the panel said it was on. If you had chosen which inboxes to watch and later reconnected those accounts, the saved choice pointed at accounts that no longer existed. It watches all of them now, and says so.
    • The Activity log, on the agent's Setup tab, now says what your email watching is actually doing: which inboxes it is watching, when it is taking its first look at a mailbox and holding back everything already sitting in there, and when it has lost track of one. The first look is what catches people out. Send yourself a test message before it happens and that message is already behind, so nothing arrives and nothing is wrong.
    • Fixed: pressing Draft on an email your agent had decided needed no reply did nothing at all. It asked itself the same question again and got the same answer. Pressing Draft is your decision, so it writes the draft now.
    • Fixed: Text Replies could go quiet with nothing wrong. A sign-in that had expired, or a dropped connection, looked exactly like a text that needed no answer.
    • Fixed: a summary sent to Telegram could arrive with stray underscores through it, once summaries became long enough to run to a second line.
    • Fixed: replacing the token for a chat app your agent is already on emptied the list of who is allowed to message it, and the screen said the opposite. It now names who would have to claim the agent again, before you press save, and sends you to the claim code afterward.
    • Fixed: a question about what was said on a past call could be handed to your calendar instead of to the add-on that reads call transcripts.
    • Fixed: the video skills could not run on any computer that downloaded their tools rather than building them, which is every computer but a developer's. Video Synthesizer works again.
    Archie 0.1.7August 25, 2026
    • Your agent now says when it cannot read a mailbox, instead of looking healthy and going quiet. A sign-in that has lapsed, or a permission your workplace withdrew, turns the agent's status to "Needs attention" and names the address, what the mail provider said, and where to press Reconnect.
    • Your agent also says when it wrote a reply and could not deliver it. A bot removed from a group, or one whose permission to post was taken away, used to look exactly like an agent with nothing to say.
    • Every connected email account has a Reconnect button now, not only the ones that could be given more access. An account that had stopped working looked perfect and had nothing to press, and the only way back was to remove it and add it again, which no screen said.
    • Fixed: connecting a calendar from inside a skill took away that account's email. It asked for calendar permission alone, and Outlook and Gmail both hand back exactly what was asked for, so everything else was dropped. It now asks for what the account already had as well.
    • Fixed: your agent could stop reading email entirely after you reconnected an account. Reconnecting changed the account's identity behind the scenes, so the list of inboxes to watch pointed at nothing, and the watcher ran every five minutes on no inboxes at all while the panel said it was on.
    • Fixed, on a shared agent: reconnecting a mailbox that belonged to one person handed it back to everybody, so their mail started arriving in the conversation the team shares.
    • Fixed: a saved thing named with an accent, like a subscription called "Uber" with the umlaut, could stop all email checking until Archie was restarted. Nothing was shown when it happened.
    • Fixed: the chat inside Archie could show a green Live badge and refuse every message you typed, after the agent restarted itself. It now keeps working, and an agent that stops on its own says so instead of claiming to be running.
    • Fixed: removing a Google account from an agent that also had Outlook could break Google Tasks days later, with nothing connecting the two.
    • Fixed: removing the last inbox you had chosen to watch started watching all of them, including other people's on a shared agent.
    • Fixed: a light whose bridge no longer accepted Archie's key was reported as a missing light, so you went looking for a lamp that was exactly where you left it.
    • Fixed: learning your writing style from your sent mail could, over the following weeks, run an Outlook sign-in down until it stopped working.
    Archie 0.1.6August 25, 2026
    • A mailbox your agent could not read is now reported as exactly that, with what the mail provider said about it. An expired sign-in, a permission a workplace withdrew, or Outlook having a bad minute all used to arrive looking identical to a quiet morning: "the inbox is empty".
    • Connecting an email account opens the mailbox once, straight away, while you are still sitting there. If it will not open, nothing is connected and the screen says what the provider said, instead of leaving a green row that never works.
    • Your agent no longer insists it can read a mailbox that has never once opened. It used to be told to say it had access on the strength of the permissions alone, so it argued with people whose mail it genuinely could not reach.
    • An Outlook account at a company or school whose administrator has to approve Archie now names the setting to ask for, spelled the way their admin console spells it, and where it lives. Asking an IT department to "approve an app called Archie" gets a reply asking which permission and where.
    • The calendar is offered whichever email you use. That button was tied to Google being configured, so somebody connecting Outlook was never offered a calendar at all.
    • Searching the store for "outlook" finds the email and calendar add-ons. Every one of them names both providers now, and Email Manager and Calendar answer to "outlook" spoken aloud as well.
    • The store says which add-ons need an AI account of your own on the row, before you press Install, rather than refusing after you have pressed it.
    • Two guides that did not exist. One is how to update Archie. The other is connecting your email and calendar: where the button is, what each permission lets your agent do, what to send a workplace administrator when it refuses, and what to do when an account stops working.
    • The first-run screens say what Archie needs to run: this computer left awake and plugged into power, with the sleep setting named and where to change it, and a cable from your router if you can reach one. A routine set for 7:30am needs this computer awake at 7:30am.
    • "Needs attention" is a button. It was two words beside a small icon whose only explanation was a tooltip, so there was nothing to press and, on a touchscreen, nothing to read.
    • Six screens sent you to Settings to connect an email or calendar account. That is not where it is. They name the Connections tab, the section inside it, and the button, and they say to tick the permissions before you sign in.
    • Fixed: an error that said only that something had failed now says where to go and what to press. A refused key names the screen you paste it into; a lost connection names the cable to check.
    • Fixed: running out of credit on your own AI account names that company and its billing page. It used to send you to a company you may not have an account with.

    • Reminders arrive with something to do about them. Done ticks the matching task off your list, Later offers an hour from now, this evening or tomorrow morning, and Dismiss closes it. Answering in words still works: say "did that" or "move it to four" and the buttons settle themselves.
    • Ask to be reminded and you get a reminder. It used to write a task instead, which is a row you have to go and look at and interrupts nobody. Now it sets the reminder, adds the task where the thing is also work worth writing down, and tells you it did both.
    • Cancel a reminder by what it is about ("cancel the invoice one") rather than by a number you were never shown. The task it was filed with goes with it.

    • A connected account that nothing is using now says so, and names the add-ons that would use it. Connecting your email and getting nothing out of it was invisible before.
    • Every setup that ends in a long code now begins by saying where to stand. Telegram gets a step of its own, because reading a 46-character token off a phone and typing it into a laptop is the part that goes wrong.     • Fixed: a task list saved by an earlier version was invisible to the agent that kept it, which then said its tools were not working.
    • Fixed: your agent sometimes answered "I processed the request but couldn't generate a response".
    • Fixed: a moment of bad network was reported as a failure and left you to send the message again.
    • Fixed: the AI account panel showed Claude selected while saying OpenAI was connected.
    • Fixed: the strip above the message box showed the raw asterisks and link addresses of the message you were replying to.

    • Its page opens on what arrived: each ability named, with what it does, and how to take any of them back off.

    • Dark mode is stone rather than brown, and every color in the app was measured against its background so nothing is left faint.
    • On Windows: the media tools (transcription, video) install on Windows now, and this is the first version Windows can update itself from.
    • Fixed: sixteen routines woke up every morning to work out whether it was their day. They run on the day they mean now.
    • Fixed: a restart could overwrite your agent's first message, and a long reply stopped one message short of the bottom of the window.
    Archie 0.1.1July 27, 2026
    • Archie updates itself. When a new version is ready, a banner appears in the app; one click downloads it, verifies it, and restarts.
    • A much smaller download. Media tools (video, transcription) now download only when you install a skill that needs them, instead of shipping inside every copy.
    • Bug fixes and stability improvements across sign-in and the marketplace.
